page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-8 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance within the Standard family. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs running on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor architecture at a base clock frequency of 3.6 GHz. Operating with one thread per physical core, the configuration delivers 2 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU.

The instance provides dedicated compute resource allocation, eliminating multi-tenant CPU contention on its assigned cores. It does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on external block volumes for persistent disk storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance deployment.

With its energy-efficient Arm64 architecture and balanced compute-to-memory allocation, VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-8 delivers a cost-efficient profile for workloads compiled for aarch64. The instance is suited for general purpose cloud workloads, including containerized microservices, development and testing environments, web serving, lightweight application backends, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-8 is a general purpose compute instance built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. Powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors clocked at 3.6 GHz, the server provides 2 dedicated vCPUs corresponding directly to 2 physical cores with single-threaded execution. It features 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage disks or GPU acceleration, and it comes provisioned with a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Its dedicated core allocation prevents noisy-neighbor CPU degradation while preserving predictable processing efficiency. With its balanced resources and power-efficient Arm core design, VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-8 provides a cost-effective operational foundation for Arm-compatible general workloads, such as lightweight web servers, microservice hosting, routine continuous integration tasks, and mid-tier backend services.
